name: Good King Henry
family: Amaranthaceae, the amaranth and goosefoot family
grown_as: A hardy perennial pot-herb: young shoots eaten like asparagus in spring, leaves like spinach later. Long called Chenopodium bonus-henricus, as William's records give it. No variety.
habit: A leafy clump 30 to 60 cm tall and about 45 cm across from a thick fleshy rootstock, with upright, little-branched stems.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate up the stems and in a loose cluster from the base
leaf.outline: Triangular to broadly arrow-shaped, 5 to 10 cm long
leaf.base: Broad and arrow-shaped, with two short pointed lobes spreading outwards
leaf.margin: Smooth or slightly wavy, no teeth
leaf.veins: A midrib with a few side veins running out towards the base lobes
leaf.surface: Slightly fleshy; young leaves mealy and a little sticky, especially beneath, so they look frosted; older leaves smoother above
leaf.stalk: Long, often as long as the blade
leaf.colour: Dark green above, paler and mealy beneath

flower.form: Tiny green flowers without petals, packed into narrow upright spikes
flower.petals: None: four or five small green tepals
flower.centre: Four or five tiny yellow stamens
flower.carried: In dense clusters making narrow, leafless, upright, tapering spikes at the stem tips and in the upper leaf joints

fruit: A tiny, round, glossy black seed about 2 mm, held in the dried flower. The spikes turn dull red-brown as they ripen.
seedling: Two narrow oblong seed leaves, mealy, then small triangular true leaves on long stalks, mealy beneath.
winter: Dies right down to the ground. In late winter fat pinkish-green shoots push up from the crown.

leaf: a triangular, arrow-shaped leaf with two short lobes spreading out at the base
a long stalk; a mealy, frosted look beneath
bloom: packed into a narrow upright spike
seedling: the first true leaves small and triangular
young: a low clump of long-stalked triangular leaves
crop: a leafy clump 30 to 60 cm of dark green arrow-shaped leaves
young shoots at the top for picking
flower: narrow, leafless, upright spikes of green flowers at the stem tips
dormant: fat pinkish-green shoots just pushing up in late winter

look_alikes: Fat hen (Chenopodium album) is an annual with grey mealy, diamond-shaped, toothed leaves and leafy flower spikes. Oraches have toothed or hooked leaf bases and flat discs round the seeds. Lords-and-ladies has a glossy arrow-shaped leaf but no mealiness and a net of veins.
